what_worked: Consistent visual identity with clean palette; the popularity-vs-value framing was a promising analytical direction.
fix_next: Replace every fabricated percentage with actual dataset calculations, disclose the 1,000-row sample, and acknowledge missingness rates.
verdict: Polished marketing pitch built on fabricated numbers, not a data story.
factual_error_detail: Slide 3: '6,000+ startups' misrepresents 1,000-row sample; '85%+ revenue-validated' unverifiable. Slide 4: Category names invented (SaaS & Productivity 35%, AI-Powered 28%, etc.) — actual top category is AI at 197/726≈27% of non-missing, but other groupings don't match. Slide 5: 'Subscriptions 65%' is not a dataset category; AI at 20% revenue share is wrong (actual AI share ≈15.1%). Slide 6: AI median '$2K–$5K' vs actual $503; SaaS median '$8K–$25K' vs actual $200.50; 'top 5% generate 40%' — actual top-10 share is 49.6% so top-5% claim is unverified/likely wrong. Slide 7: Geographic percentages (US 35% listings/45% revenue) appear invented — no match to dataset. Slide 8: Stripe 72% vs actual 636/1000=63.6%; RevenueCat 12% vs actual 189/1000=18.9%; Polar 8% not verifiable as named 'Dodo' at 5%. '60% revenue from US/UK/Canada' unverifiable with 241 missing countries.

evidence.insight: Core ideas (AI maturity gap, concentration risk) are directionally interesting but built on fabricated numbers, rendering them hollow. No analysis of anonymity premium, TLD signals, sale multiples, or missingness patterns.
evidence.narrative: Loose arc from model→composition→revenue→geography→infrastructure→strategy exists but reads as a consulting pitch for TrustMRR rather than a critical, thesis-driven data story. No hypothesis tested or tension resolved.
evidence.framing: Never identifies the 1,000-row sample; implies coverage of 6,000+ startups. Zero mention of missingness (241 country, 274 category, 288 audience_type). No limitations, no source citation. Cold reader would be misled about scope.
evidence.accuracy: Nearly every quantitative claim departs from the frozen reference. Categories renamed/merged without disclosure. Median MRR figures inflated 4–50x. Payment provider shares wrong. Geographic data appears wholly invented. Revenue-by-category chart uses 'Subscriptions' which doesn't exist in the dataset.
evidence.visual: Cohesive dark teal + coral palette, legible type, clean chart formatting. Three donut charts become repetitive. Decorative clip-art on slides 1, 2, 9 adds no analytical value. Charts are well-rendered but encode fabricated data.
evidence.ai_slop: Heavy AI-generated indicators: identical slide templates, decorative clip-art, inflated consulting language ('category of one,' 'network effects'), suspiciously round percentages (35/28/15/12/10), no evidence of actual data manipulation or code.

change_reason: Lowered insight 2.5→2.0 (no genuine dataset analysis underpins any claim) and accuracy 1.5→1.0 (identified additional fabricated figures including median MRR off by 4–50x and invented geographic data); lowered framing 3→2.5 (actively misleading about dataset scope). Visual and narrative unchanged.
